connection: Session 25 supplies the required foundation. This session extends TimeClock with async composition while keeping execution observable and deterministic.
objectives: Explain why awaiting in sequence preserves ordering while Task.WhenAll allows independent operations to make progress together.
Trace the operation across its execution or application boundary.
Implement the focused sequential and concurrent asynchronous flow lab.
Verify success and failure behavior with automated checks.

concept.title: Use the accurate execution model
paragraphs: The governing rule is that awaiting in sequence preserves ordering while Task.WhenAll allows independent operations to make progress together.
Avoid equating an abstraction with one possible implementation detail; reason from its documented contract.

concept.title: Keep boundaries explicit
paragraphs: Dependencies, cancellation, persistence, and transport values should cross named boundaries.
This makes ownership clear and supplies seams for deterministic tests.
concept.code:
// The boundary exposes intent.
ClockEntry[] entries = await Task.WhenAll(loads);

concept.title: Verify observable outcomes
paragraphs: Focused tests control inputs and collaborators so timing and failure assertions stay stable.
The full suite checks that new infrastructure has not weakened the domain model.

lab.objective: Implement one production-sized slice demonstrating sequential and concurrent asynchronous flow.
lab.startingCondition: Sessions 01–25 are complete and the solution is green.
steps: Predict one success outcome and one failure, cancellation, or boundary outcome.
Add the implementation centered on EntryBatchLoader.cs.
Add EntryBatchLoaderTests.cs with deterministic Arrange–Act–Assert checks.
Run the focused checks and inspect the relevant returned value or state.
Run the full Release build, test suite, and site validator.
lab.expectedBehavior: The checks establish that awaiting in sequence preserves ordering while Task.WhenAll allows independent operations to make progress together; all earlier tests continue to pass.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeClock.sln --configuration Release

commit: session-26: teach sequential and concurrent async flow
review: The abstraction is not confused with one runtime implementation.
Inputs and dependencies cross explicit boundaries.
Async methods return Task and accept cancellation where relevant.
Persistence and HTTP models remain separate from domain objects.
Tests are deterministic and cover a meaningful failure path.
The complete solution builds without warnings.

postQuiz.prompt: What did this session establish about sequential and concurrent asynchronous flow?
options: awaiting in sequence preserves ordering while Task.WhenAll allows independent operations to make progress together
The compiler removes all failure cases
Every boundary should use the same concrete type
postQuiz.explanation: The implementation and tests demonstrate the stated contract.

postQuiz.prompt: Where is an asynchronous exception observed?
options: When its faulted task is awaited
Only when a thread is manually created
postQuiz.explanation: Await unwraps and rethrows the task failure at the awaiting boundary.

postQuiz.prompt: Why separate transport or persistence models from domain behavior?
options: Each boundary can evolve without distorting domain invariants
postQuiz.explanation: Mapping keeps responsibilities and change reasons distinct.

reflections: Which assumption about async composition did the executable example confirm or correct?
Where does failure cross the boundary, and who should handle it?
Which dependency can a test replace with a controlled implementation?
whatBreaks: Removing EntryBatchLoader.cs removes the canonical example for async composition. Removing its tests makes timing, failure, persistence, or HTTP behavior easier to regress. Hiding the boundary behind global state would also make the behavior harder to observe and control.
summary: This session established that awaiting in sequence preserves ordering while Task.WhenAll allows independent operations to make progress together. Explicit boundaries and deterministic checks make the application behavior dependable.
